title: Scheduling & Operational Automation: Cron and systemd Timers
purpose: Eight connected offline scheduler exercises. Sequence guides practice, not a forced unlock.
prerequisites: Earlier Bash, users/groups and service-unit skills; unchanged approved administrator image. No at, credentials, networking or clock changes.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 107.2 partial; 105.2/108.2 and LPIC-2 v4.5 202.1 reinforcement only. At/access policies and full coverage remain missing. Self-reviewed, unscored.

entries.description: Separate schedule, clock, loaded limits and job identity.
materials: Guest-only administration: sudo, never host administration. No learner/root credentials, sudoers, account-policy, networking or clock changes. Lessons are display-only; the app does not execute these instructions.

Begin on a fresh lesson disk. Stop on name/path/unit/crontab collisions. Inspect and clean only your exact disposable fixture before repeating; never adopt another account or replace an unrelated crontab.
Enter the short printf lines manually or use the installed vi. No clipboard sharing is assumed.
observations: Retain date/timezone, tools, loaded state and actual ll-s1 id.
Distinguish trigger, process exit and valid report.
questions: Who runs cron itself versus a user-crontab command?
limitations: Self-reviewed, unscored. A timer trigger is not proof of job success: inspect exit status, execution identity, output owner and contents.
Guest root can override guest-side limits. At is absent; no at, cron access-policy, mail delivery, DST or complete LPIC coverage.
Resume boots disk state, not RAM/jobs. VM disks/reports are excluded from profile backups; retain observations before confirmed Reset.
cleanup: Inspect sudo crontab -u ll-s1 -l. If it contains only your practice entry, sudo crontab -u ll-s1 -r. This prevents future runs, not an already-running job.

Inspect pgrep -u ll-s1 -a; wait for your bounded job to finish. Only when no processes remain: sudo userdel -r ll-s1. Verify ! getent passwd ll-s1; test ! -e /home/ll-s1. Repeat cleanup conditionally; never remove learner.
troubleshooting: Check LoadState=loaded before trusting configured properties. A collected transient unit can report defaults.
Check identity, absolute paths, environment and output access; root success is not job-account success.
On interruption stop only the named timer, inspect its exact service/process, wait for bounded work and perform exact cleanup. No broad process termination.

entries.description: Repair lookup and executable access under cron environment.

Challenge starting conditions only, not repairs:
! getent passwd ll-s4 && ! getent group ll-s4 && test ! -e /home/ll-s4 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-s4
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin 'umask 077' 'cd /home/ll-s4 || exit 3' 'report-helper > report.txt' | sudo tee /home/ll-s4/job.sh > /dev/null && sudo chown ll-s4:ll-s4 /home/ll-s4/job.sh && sudo chmod 0700 /home/ll-s4/job.sh
sudo runuser -u ll-s4 -- mkdir /home/ll-s4/bin; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'printf "user=%s\n" "$(id -un)"' | sudo tee /home/ll-s4/bin/report-helper > /dev/null && sudo chown ll-s4:ll-s4 /home/ll-s4/bin/report-helper && sudo chmod 0600 /home/ll-s4/bin/report-helper
sudo test ! -e /var/spool/cron/crontabs/ll-s4 && printf '%s\n' 'MAILTO=""' 'SHELL=/bin/sh' 'PATH=/usr/bin:/bin' '* * * * * umask 077; /usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 5s /home/ll-s4/job.sh > /home/ll-s4/stdout.txt 2> /home/ll-s4/error.txt; echo $? > /home/ll-s4/status.txt' | sudo crontab -u ll-s4 -; end=$((SECONDS+85)); until sudo test -s /home/ll-s4/error.txt; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; sudo cat /home/ll-s4/error.txt
